Regulation of the Securities Business Segment
paragraphs: Our Company is a technology-driven, diversified financial services company with approximately $30.0 billion in assets and approximately $47.8 billion of assets under custody and/or administration at Axos Clearing LLC ("Axos Clearing"). Our client-centric, technology-enabled services model provides secure and scalable banking, clearing and custody, and investment advisory solutions to retail and business customers. The Bank provides consumer and commercial banking products and services through its digital online and mobile banking platforms, low-cost distribution channels and affinity partners. Our Bank offers deposit and lending products to customers nationwide including consumer and business checking, savings and time deposit accounts and single family and multifamily residential mortgages, commercial real estate mortgages and loans, lender finance loans, asset-based loans, capital call facilities, equipment lending and leasing, auto loans, retail and floor plan marine loans and other consumer loans. Our Bank generates non-interest income from consumer and business products and services, including fees from loans originated for sale, operating lease income, deposit account service fees, prepayment fees, loan servicing fees, as well as technology and payment transaction processing fees, among others. We offer securities products and services to independent registered investment advisors ("RIAs") and introducing broker-dealers ("IBDs") through Axos Clearing and Axos Advisor Services ("AAS") and direct-to-consumer securities trading and digital investment management products through Axos Invest, Inc. ("Axos Invest"). AAS and Axos Clearing generate interest and asset- and transaction-based fee income by providing comprehensive securities custody services to RIAs and clearing, stock lending, and margin lending services to IBDs respectively. Axos Invest generates fee income from self-directed securities trading and digital wealth management services. Our common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "AX" and is a component of the Russell 2000® Index and the S&P SmallCap 600® Index, among other indices.

We conduct business primarily through two operating segments: the Banking Business Segment and the Securities Business Segment. For additional information on our business segments, see Note 23—"Segment Reporting" in the Consolidated Financial Statements.

We distribute our loan products through our retail, correspondent and wholesale channels. The loans we retain primarily include first mortgages secured by single family real property, multifamily real property and commercial real property, commercial & industrial loans and leases to businesses, automobile loans and certain other consumer loans. We also invest in debt securities to manage liquidity and interest rate risk. Because risk-adjusted returns available on acquired assets may exceed returns available through retaining assets from our origination channels, we have elected to purchase loans and securities from time to time, and may continue to do so in the future. Our deposit products are sourced from a wide range of retail and commercial distribution channels, and our deposits consist of demand, savings and time deposits.

Our Single Family - Mortgage & Warehouse loans are primarily secured by first liens on 1-4 unit residential properties. Loans include fixed- and adjustable-rate single family residential mortgages and home equity lines of credit. We source single family mortgage loans through mortgage brokers, mortgage bankers, financial institutions and direct to consumer.

Our adjustable-rate loans have initial fixed-rate periods, generally five, seven, or ten years, before starting a variable rate period, and may also have interest rate floors, ceilings and rate change caps.
We also warehouse certain loans for independent mortgage bankers to sell to investors and government agencies.

Our Multifamily and Commercial Mortgage loans are primarily secured by multifamily real estate or commercial real estate. Loans often include initial fixed rate periods of either three, five, or seven years before starting a variable rate period, which is based on the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") or other interest rate indices. Multifamily and commercial mortgage loans generally include prepayment protection clauses, interest floors and rate change caps. We source multifamily and commercial mortgage loans through targeted direct-to-borrower origination channels and we may sell certain loans to investors.

Our Commercial Real Estate ("CRE") loans are secured by real estate properties in a variety of structures. CRE loans include our CRE specialty loans, real estate lender finance loans, as well as other CRE loans that may be collateralized directly by real estate or indirectly by loans secured by real estate. We source our CRE loans through direct-to-borrower originations, brokers, and third-party lenders.
Our commercial real estate loans generally have a variable rate, which is generally based on SOFR, as well as prepayment protection clauses, interest rate floors and rate change caps.
Commercial & Industrial - Non-Real Estate ("non-RE")

Our commercial & industrial – non-RE loans are typically secured by commercial assets, including, but not limited to, receivables, inventory, equipment and other assets as included in related uniform commercial code ("UCC") all asset filings. Product types include lender finance, asset-based loans, leveraged cash flow loans, insurance premium finance, capital call facilities, equipment loans and leases, floor plan loans, and general working capital commercial and industrial loans. We source commercial & industrial – non-RE loans through direct-to-borrower origination and through third-party sales referrals.

Our commercial & industrial – non-RE loans generally have a variable rate based on SOFR or other interest rate indices, as well as prepayment protection clauses, interest rate floors and rate change caps. Our equipment leases typically have fixed rates. For certain commercial non-real estate loan products, we typically reduce risk exposure in these loans by entering into a structured facility, under which we take a senior lien position collateralized by the underlying assets at advance rates well below the collateral value. Leveraged cash flow loans rely on free cash flow as a primary repayment source and enterprise value as the secondary repayment source. The liquidation of collateral in the event of a borrower default may be an insufficient source of repayment because accounts or loans receivable may be uncollectible and inventories and equipment may be obsolete or of limited use. We attempt to mitigate these risks through the structuring of these lending products, adhering to underwriting policies in evaluating the management of the business and the creditworthiness of borrowers and guarantors.

Our Auto loans are secured by new and used automobiles ("auto") and are sourced primarily through indirect channels. Originations are prime credit quality with a fixed interest rate and terms ranging from three to eight years. We retain and service auto originations.
Our Consumer loans are fixed rate, unsecured loans to well-qualified, individual borrowers sourced through existing bank customers, lead aggregators and other marketing efforts.

paragraphs: An investment in our common stock is subject to risks inherent in our business. Before making an investment decision, you should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all of the other information included in this report. In addition to the risks and uncertainties described below, other risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or that we currently deem to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. Risks disclosed in this section may have already materialized. The value or market price of our common stock could decline due to any of these identified or other risks, and you could lose all or part of your investment. This report is qualified in its entirety by these risk factors.
Changes in interest rates could adversely affect our performance.

Our results of operations depend to a great extent on our net interest income, which is the difference between the interest earned on interest-earning assets such as loans and investment securities, and the interest paid on interest-bearing liabilities such as deposits and borrowings. We are exposed to interest rate risk because our interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities do not react uniformly or concurrently to changes in interest rates, as they may have different time periods for adjustment and can be tied to different measures of rates. Interest rates are sensitive to factors that are beyond our control, including domestic and international economic conditions, including inflation, and the policies of various governmental and regulatory agencies, including the Federal Reserve. The monetary policies of the Federal Reserve, implemented through open market operations, the federal funds rate ("Fed Funds Rate") targets, and the discount rate for banking borrowings and reserve requirements, affect prevailing interest rates. A material change in any of these policies could have a material impact on us or our customers (including borrowers), and therefore on our results of operations.

Loan originations and repayment rates tend to increase with declining interest rates and decrease with rising interest rates. Increases in interest rates can negatively impact our business, including a possible reduction in customers' or potential customers' desire to borrow money or adversely affecting customers' ability to repay on outstanding loans by increasing their debt obligations. On the deposit side, increasing interest rates generally lead to higher rates paid for our deposit accounts. While we manage the sensitivity of our assets and liabilities, large, unanticipated, or rapid increases in market interest rates may have an adverse impact on our net interest income and could decrease our mortgage refinancing business and related fee income, and could cause an increase in delinquencies and non-performing loans and leases in our adjustable-rate loans. In addition, interest rate volatility can affect the value of our loans and leases, investments and other interest-rate sensitive assets and our ability to realize gains on the sale or resolution of these assets, which in turn may affect our liquidity. Although we have implemented risk management strategies, as well as policies and procedures designed to manage the risks associated with changes in market interest rates, there can be no assurance that we will be able to successfully manage our interest rate risk. If borrower or depositor behavior or overall economic conditions in the future are significantly different than we anticipate, then our risk mitigation may be insufficient to protect against interest rate risk and our operating results and financial condition could be adversely affected.

A significant or sustained economic downturn could result in increases in our level of non-performing loans and leases and/or reduce demand for our products and services, which could have an adverse effect on our results of operations.

Our business and results of operations are affected by the financial markets and general economic conditions, including factors such as the level and volatility of interest rates, inflation, home prices, unemployment and under-employment levels, bankruptcies, household income and consumer spending. We operate in an uncertain economic environment due to a variety of other reasons including, but not limited to, trade policies and disputes, tariffs, geopolitical tensions and global military conflicts, including the Russia-Ukraine war and conflicts in the Middle East, inflation, fluctuating commodity prices and volatile global supply chains and energy market prices and disruptions. The risks associated with our business become more acute in periods of a slowing economy or slow growth. Furthermore, given our high concentration of loans secured by real estate in California and New York, the Company remains particularly susceptible to a downturn in those states' economies.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements that are based upon current expectations. Forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results and the timing of events could differ materially from those expressed or implied in our forward-looking statements due to various important factors, including those set forth under "Risk Factors" in Item 1A. and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. The following discussion and analysis should be read together with the Consolidated Financial Statements, including the related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

The Consolidated Financial Statements include the accounts of Axos Financial, Inc. ("Axos") and its wholly owned subsidiaries, Axos Bank (the "Bank" or "Axos Bank") and Axos Nevada Holding, LLC ("Axos Nevada Holding"), collectively, the "Company." Axos, the Bank, three lending-related entities and Axos Nevada Holding comprise substantially all of the Company's assets and liabilities and revenues and expenses. The Bank, its wholly owned subsidiaries, three lending-related entities and certain other lending activities constitute the Banking Business Segment. Axos Nevada Holding owns Axos Securities, LLC, which owns Axos Clearing LLC ("Axos Clearing"), a clearing broker-dealer, Axos Invest, Inc., a registered investment advisor, and Axos Invest LLC, an introducing broker-dealer. Axos Securities, LLC and its consolidated subsidiaries constitute the Securities Business Segment. Axos Bank provides consumer and business banking products through its low-cost distribution channels and affinity partners. Axos Clearing and Axos Invest LLC, provide comprehensive securities clearing services to introducing broker-dealers and registered investment advisor correspondents and digital investment advisory services to retail investors, respectively. Axos Financial, Inc.'s common stock is listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol "AX" and is a component of the Russell 2000® Index and the S&P SmallCap 600® Index, among other indices.

From time to time, we undertake acquisitions or similar transactions consistent with our operating and growth strategies. On August 23, 2023, the Company acquired approximately $52 million of marine floor financing loans at par value along with other assets for an additional $2 million, primarily consisting of servicing rights as well as certain employees. The transaction was accounted for as an asset acquisition and such assets are included in the Company's Consolidated Balance Sheets.

On December 7, 2023, the Company acquired from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation ("FDIC") two loan portfolios, comprising both purchased credit deteriorated ("PCD") and non-PCD loans, with an aggregate unpaid principal balance of $1.3 billion at a fair value of $901.5 million, reflecting a non-credit-related discount of $306.8 million and an allowance for credit losses on PCD loans of $70.1 million, (the "FDIC Loan Purchase"). Also included in the acquisition were certain related interest rate derivative assets and liabilities with a fair value of $109.0 million and $104.4 million, respectively, as of the date of the acquisition and whose maturities generally align with those of the loans acquired. The acquisition of the non-PCD loans and interest rate derivatives was accounted for as a purchase of financial assets and liabilities, and the Company recognized a $92.4 million gain on the transaction included in "Gain on acquisition" in the Consolidated Statement of Income.

On September 30, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of the membership interests in Verdant Commercial Capital, LLC ("Verdant") in an all-cash transaction, which increases the Company's scale and enhances the Company's existing equipment leasing business. As part of the acquisition, the Company acquired, among other assets and liabilities, approximately $1.0 billion of loans and leases (including $211.0 million of PCD assets) and $212.6 million of equipment under operating lease arrangements.

On January 23, 2026, the Company purchased a multi-building commercial office complex and associated amenities located in San Diego, California for approximately $125 million, which Axos Bank intends to occupy as its headquarters in the future.

On April 22, 2026, the Bank entered into a purchase and assumption agreement with Capital One, National Association to acquire approximately $3.2 billion of deposits, comprising IRA savings and IRA certificate of deposit accounts. The deposit acquisition was approved by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on June 8, 2026, and is expected to close in calendar year 2026.

On May 2, 2026, the Bank completed its previously announced acquisition of all of the United States consumer deposits of Jenius Bank, a digital banking business of SMBC MANUBANK ("SMBC"), pursuant to the terms of the Purchase and Assumption Agreement, dated February 12, 2026. The Bank acquired approximately $2.3 billion of deposits from Jenius Bank and received cash, less a negotiated premium.
For additional information on these acquisitions, see Note 2—"Acquisitions." There were no other significant acquisitions during fiscal years 2026, 2025 or 2024.

The following discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations is based upon our Consolidated Financial Statements and the notes thereto, which have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP"). The preparation of these Consolidated Financial Statements requires us to make a number of estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts and disclosures in the Consolidated Financial Statements. On an ongoing basis, we evaluate our estimates and assumptions based upon historical experience and various factors and circumstances. We believe that our estimates and assumptions are reasonable under the circumstances. However, actual results may differ significantly from these estimates and assumptions that could have a material effect on the carrying value of assets and liabilities at the balance sheet dates and our results of operations for the reporting periods.

Critical accounting estimates are those that we consider most important to the portrayal of our financial condition and results of operations because they require our most difficult judgments, often as a result of the need to make estimates that are inherently uncertain. We have identified critical accounting policies and estimates below. In addition, these critical accounting estimates are discussed further in Note 1—"Organizations and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" in the Consolidated Financial Statements.

Allowance for Credit Losses. The Company maintains an allowance for credit losses ("ACL") for its held-for-investment loan and net investment in leases portfolio as well as lending commitments, excluding loans measured at fair value in accordance with applicable accounting standards, which represents management's estimate of the expected lifetime credit losses on the loans and net investment in leases. The estimate of the allowance for credit losses includes both a quantitative and qualitative assessment, both of which include variables that are subject to uncertainty.

The quantitative assessment reflects modeled outputs utilizing economic scenarios and forecasts, which are subject to uncertainty, and is also based on the Company's current and expected future economic outlook. Key economic variables considered in the quantitative assessment include factors such as the U.S. unemployment rate and interest rates, both of which impact the default rate of the loan pools. Additionally, the results of the quantitative assessment are impacted by the third-party macroeconomic forecasts across various economic scenarios. The Company periodically reviews and adjusts the weighting of scenarios based on management's ACL framework. Adjustment of scenario weighting away from the baseline scenario to the adverse scenario should increase the ACL on the Company's held-for-investment loan and net investment in leases portfolio, all else remaining equal. Economic forecasts that impacted management's assessment of scenario weightings included, among other forecasts, interest rates, inflation, changes in trade policies, and geopolitical unrest. Changes in one or more of these variables can cause a significant change in the estimate of the ACL.

Additionally, management performs a qualitative assessment to address inherent limitations in the model and data. Qualitative criteria used in the assessment, as outlined in Note 1—"Organizations and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies" in the Consolidated Financial Statements, can require significant judgment and is subject to uncertainty.

paragraphs: 本公司為一間以科技為驅動、多元化財務服務公司，截至 Axos Clearing LLC（"Axos Clearing"）的資產約為 300 億美元，資產保管及/或管理的資產約為 478 億美元。我們以客戶為中心、以科技為基礎的服務模式，為零售與企業客戶提供安全且可擴展的銀行、清算與保管、以及投資顧問解決方案。銀行透過其數位線上與行動銀行平台、低成本分銷渠道與親善夥伴，提供消費者與企業銀行產品與服務。我們的銀行向全國客戶提供存款與貸款產品，包括消費者與企業支票存款、儲蓄與定期存款帳戶，以及單戶與多戶住宅抵押貸款、商業不動產抵押貸款與貸款、貸款人融資貸款、以資產為基礎的貸款、資本調用設施、設備貸款與租賃、汽車貸款、零售與地板計劃船隻貸款及其他消費者貸款。我們的銀行透過消費者與企業產品與服務產生非利息收入，包括貸款發放後出售的費用、經營租賃收入、存款帳戶服務費用、預付款費用、貸款服務費用，以及科技與支付交易處理費用等。我們透過 Axos Clearing 和 Axos Advisor Services（"AAS"）以及 Axos Invest, Inc.（"Axos Invest"）向獨立註冊投資顧問（"RIAs"）與介紹經紀商（"IBDs"）提供證券產品與服務，並透過 Axos Invest 提供直接對消費者證券交易與數位投資管理產品。AAS 和 Axos Clearing 透過為 RIAs 提供全面證券保管服務，以及為 IBDs 提供清算、股票貸款與 margin 貸款服務，產生利息與資產及交易相關費用收入。Axos Invest 透過自導式證券交易與數位財富管理服務產生費用收入。本公司普通股在紐約證券交易所上市，股票代碼為 "AX"，並為 Russell 2000® 指數與 S&P SmallCap 600® 指數等其他指數的組成部分。
我們主要透過兩個營運分部進行業務：銀行業務分部與證券業務分部。如需更多有關我們業務分部的資訊，請參閱財務報表附註 23—"分部報告"。

我們透過零售、 correspondent 及 wholesale 渠道分銷貸款產品。我們保留的貸款主要包括以單戶住宅不動產、多戶住宅不動產及商業不動產為抵押的第一順位抵押貸款、商業與工業貸款及租賃貸款給企業、汽車貸款及某些其他消費者貸款。我們也投資於債務證券以管理流動性與利率風險。由於取得資產的風險調整後回報可能高於透過我們發行渠道保留資產的回報，我們已選擇不時購買貸款與證券，並可能在未來繼續進行此舉。我們的存款產品來自廣泛的零售與商業分銷渠道，我們的存款包括活期存款、儲蓄存款與定期存款。
我們的單戶住宅 - 抵押貸款與倉儲貸款主要以單戶住宅不動產的第一順位抵押為擔保。貸款包括固定利率與變動利率的單戶住宅住宅抵押貸款與住宅貸款信用線。我們透過抵押經紀商、抵押銀行、金融機構及直接對消費者取得單戶住宅抵押貸款。
我們的變動利率貸款有初始固定利率期間，通常為五年、七年或十年，之後開始變動利率期間，並可能設有利率地板、天花板及利率變動上限。
我們也為獨立抵押銀行倉儲某些貸款，以銷售給投資者與政府機構。

我們的多戶住宅與商業抵押貸款主要以多戶住宅不動產或商業不動產為擔保。貸款通常包括初始固定利率期間為三年、五年或七年，之後開始變動利率期間，該變動利率基於secured overnight financing rate（"SOFR"）或其他利率指標。多戶住宅與商業抵押貸款通常包含預付款保護條款、利率地板及利率變動上限。我們透過針對性的直接對借款人發行渠道取得多戶住宅與商業抵押貸款，並可能將某些貸款銷售給投資者。
我們的商業不動產（"CRE"）貸款以各種結構的不動產為擔保。CRE 貸款包括我們的 CRE 專業貸款、不動產貸款人融資貸款，以及可能以不動產直接擔保或間接以不動產貸款為擔保的其他 CRE 貸款。我們透過直接對借款人發行、經紀商及第三方貸款人取得 CRE 貸款。
本公司之商業不動產貸款通常為變動利率，通常以SOFR為基礎，並包含預付款保護條款、利率下限及利率變動上限。
商業及工業－非不動產（"非不動產"）
本公司之商業及工業－非不動產貸款通常以商業資產為擔保，包括但不限於應收帳款、存貨、設備及其他資產，如相關統一商業法典（"UCC"）所列之資產登記。產品類型包括貸款融資、資產擔保貸款、槓桿現金流貸款、保險 premiums 融資、資本調用融資、設備貸款及租賃、營業場地貸款及一般營運資金商業及工業貸款。本公司透過直接對借款人發放貸款及透過第三方銷售推薦來來源商業及工業－非不動產貸款。

本公司之商業及工業－非不動產貸款通常為以SOFR或其他利率指標為基礎之變動利率，並包含預付款保護條款、利率下限及利率變動上限。本公司之設備租賃通常為固定利率。對於某些商業非不動產貸款產品，本公司通常透過結構化融資安排來降低這些貸款之風險敞口，於此安排下，本公司取得對擔保資產之優先質權，且貸款額度遠低於擔保資產價值。槓桿現金流貸款依賴自由現金流作為主要償還來源，企業價值作為次要償還來源。若借款人違約，擔保品之處分可能無法提供足夠償還來源，因應收帳款或貸款可能無法收回，存貨及設備可能過時或使用有限。本公司透過這些貸款產品之結構設計、遵循授信政策評估企業管理及借款人及擔保人之信用worthiness，以緩解這些風險。
本公司之汽車貸款以新舊汽車（"汽車"）為擔保，主要透過間接渠道來來源。貸款發放為優質信用等級，為固定利率，貸款期限為三年至八年。本公司保留並處理汽車貸款發放。
本公司之消費者貸款為固定利率、無擔保貸款，提供給資格良好之個人借款人，來源為現有銀行客戶、行銷代理商及其他行銷活動。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析包含基於目前預期的向前看聲明。向前看聲明涉及風險與不確定性。本公司實際結果及事件的時程可能與向前看聲明所表達或暗示者有重大差異，原因包括多項重要因素，包括於第 1A 項「風險因素」及本年度報告表 10-K 其他地方所列述者。以下討論與分析應與合併財務報表，包括其相關附註，一併閱讀。

合併財務報表包含 Axos Financial, Inc.（"Axos"）及其全資子公司 Axos Bank（"Bank" 或 "Axos Bank"）及 Axos Nevada Holding, LLC（"Axos Nevada Holding"）的帳戶，合稱為 "本公司"。Axos、Bank、三個貸款相關實體及 Axos Nevada Holding 約佔本公司資產與負債及收入與費用的絕大部分。Bank、其全資子公司、三個貸款相關實體及某些其他貸款業務構成銀行業務分部。Axos Nevada Holding 擁有 Axos Securities, LLC，該公司擁有 Axos Clearing LLC（"Axos Clearing"），為清算經紀商，Axos Invest, Inc.，為註冊投資顧問，以及 Axos Invest LLC，為介紹經紀商。Axos Securities, LLC 及其合併子公司構成證券業務分部。Axos Bank 透過其低成本分銷渠道及親善夥伴提供消費者及企業銀行產品。Axos Clearing 及 Axos Invest LLC，分別為介紹經紀商及註冊投資顧問對應者提供綜合證券清算服務，並為零售投資者提供數位投資顧問服務。Axos Financial, Inc. 的普通股於紐約證券交易所上市，股票代碼為 "AX"，並為 Russell 2000® 指數及 S&P SmallCap 600® 指數等其他指數的組成部分。
有時本公司會進行收購或類似交易，符合本公司營運與成長策略。2023 年 8 月 23 日，本公司以票面價值約 5200 萬美元取得約 5200 萬美元的船舶地板融資貸款，並以額外 200 萬美元取得其他資產，主要為服務權及某些員工。此交易被視為資產收購，相關資產已包含於本公司合併資產負債表中。

於 2023 年 12 月 7 日，本公司自美國聯邦存款保險公司（"FDIC"）取得兩筆貸款組合，包含已購入信用惡化（"PCD"）貸款及非 PCD 貸款，其未償還本金總額為 1.3 十億美元，以公平價值 901.5 百萬美元計，反映非信用相關折讓 306.8 百萬美元，以及 PCD 貸款信用減損準備 70.1 百萬美元，（稱為 "FDIC 貸款購入"）。本次取得亦包含若干相關利率衍生資產與負債，其公平價值分別為 109.0 百萬美元與 104.4 百萬美元，於取得日計量，其到期日通常與取得貸款之到期日一致。非 PCD 貸款及利率衍生品之取得，依財務資產與負債之購入處理，本公司於交易中認列 92.4 百萬美元之獲利，計入 "取得獲利" 項目於合併損益表中。
於 2025 年 9 月 30 日，本公司完成以現金方式取得 Verdant Commercial Capital, LLC（"Verdant"） 100% 之成員權益，此交易使本公司規模擴大，並強化本公司現有設備租賃業務。本次取得包含若干資產與負債，其中約 1.0 十億美元之貸款與租賃（包含 211.0 百萬美元之 PCD 資產）及 212.6 百萬美元之設備於營運租賃安排下。
2026 年 1 月 23 日，本公司以約 1.25 億美元購入位於美國加州聖地牙哥的多棟商業辦公大樓及相關設施，Axos Bank 預計將於未來作為總部使用。
2026 年 4 月 22 日，Bank 與 Capital One, National Association 簽訂買賣協議，取得約 32 億美元存款，包含 IRA 儲蓄及 IRA 存款證書帳戶。此存款收購於 2026 年 6 月 8 日獲美國貨幣監理署批准，預計於 2026 年財務年度內完成。
2026 年 5 月 2 日，Bank 完成其先前宣佈的收購 SMBC MANUBANK（"SMBC"）旗下美國消費者存款，根據 2026 年 2 月 12 日簽訂的買賣協議。Bank 從 Jenius Bank 取得約 23 億美元存款，並收到現金，扣除協議商定的 premiums。
有關這些併購之更多資訊，請參閱附註 2—"併購"。在會計年度 2026、2025 或 2024 年間，沒有其他重大併購發生。

以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，係根據我們合併財務報表及其附註，而這些財務報表係依照美國通用會計原則（"GAAP"）編製。這些合併財務報表之編製，需要我們做出若干會影響合併財務報表中所列示金額及揭露之估計與假設。我們持續根據歷史經驗及各種因素與情況，評估這些估計與假設。我們認為在現有情況下，這些估計與假設是合理的。然而，實際結果可能與這些估計與假設有顯著差異，這可能會對資產與負債在資產負債表日的帳面價值，以及我們在報導期間的營運成果產生重大影響。
關鍵會計估計係指我們認為對我們財務狀況及營運成果之呈現最重要之估計，因為這些估計通常需要我們做出最困難的判斷，往往由於需要做出本質上不確定之估計所致。我們已識別出關鍵會計政策與估計，如下所述。此外，這些關鍵會計估計亦在合併財務報表之附註 1—"組織結構及重要會計政策摘要"中進一步討論。
信用減損準備。本公司針對其持有至到期之貸款及淨投資於租賃組合，以及貸款承諾（排除依適用會計準則以公允價值計量之貸款），維持信用減損準備（"ACL"），此準備代表管理層對貸款及淨投資於租賃之預期全生命週期信用減損之估計。信用減損準備之估計包括定量與定性評估，兩者皆包含受不確定性影響之變數。

定量評估反映經濟情境與預測之模型輸出，這些輸出受不確定性影響，並基於本公司目前及預期未來之經濟展望。定量評估中所考量之關鍵經濟變數包括美國失業率與利率，這些變數會影響貸款組合之違約率。此外，定量評估之結果亦受第三方總體經濟預測之影響，這些預測涵蓋各種經濟情境。本公司定期審查並調整各情境之權重，基於管理層之 ACL 框架。在其他條件相同的情況下，將情境權重從基準情境調整至不利情境，應會提高本公司持有至到期貸款及淨投資於租賃組合之 ACL。影響管理層評估情境權重之經濟預測包括，但不限於利率、通貨膨脹、貿易政策變動及地緣政治動盪。這些變數之一或多項之變動，可能導致 ACL 之估計產生顯著變化。
此外，管理層進行定性評估，以處理模型與數據之內在限制。在評估中所使用之定性準則，如附註 1—"組織結構及重要會計政策摘要"中所述，可能需要重大判斷，並受不確定性影響。

paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股有風險，這些風險源自於本公司業務本質。在做出投資決定前，您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本報告中包含的所有其他資訊。除了下列所描述的風險與不確定性外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前本公司尚未知悉或認為不重要，但這些風險可能對本公司業務、財務狀況與營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。本節所揭露的風險可能已經實現。本公司普通股的價值或市場價格可能因任何這些已識別或其它風險而下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。本報告中所披露的風險因素為本報告的全部內容所限定。
利率的變動可能對本公司營運表現產生不利影響。

本公司營運成果在很大程度上取決於淨利息收入，這是利息收入與利息支出之間的差額，其中利息收入來自於貸款與投資證券等利息產生資產，利息支出則來自於存款與借款等利息負債。本公司面臨利率風險，因為利息產生資產與利息負債對利率變動的反應可能不會同步或一致，因為它們可能有不同的調整週期，且可能與不同的利率指標掛鉤。利率會受到我們無法控制的多種因素影響，包括國內外經濟狀況，包括通貨膨脹，以及各政府與監管機構的政策，包括聯邦儲備系統。聯邦儲備系統透過公開市場操作、聯邦基金利率（"Fed Funds Rate"）目標以及銀行借款貼現率與準備金率等貨幣政策，影響當前利率。任何這些政策的重大變動都可能對本公司或客戶（包括借款人）產生重大影響，因此對本公司營運成果產生影響。

貸款發放與償還率通常會隨著利率下降而增加，並隨著利率上升而減少。利率上升可能對本公司業務產生負面影響，包括客戶或潛在客戶借款意願的可能減少，或因增加其債務負擔而對客戶償還現有貸款的能力產生不利影響。在存款方面，利率上升通常會導致我們存款帳戶的利率提高。雖然我們管理資產與負債的敏感度，但市場利率的重大、未預期或快速上升可能對我們的淨利息收入產生不利影響，並可能減少我們的房貸重組業務與相關費用收入，同時可能導致我們可調利率貸款的違約率與不良貸款與租賃增加。此外，利率波動可能影響我們貸款與租賃、投資及其他利率敏感性資產的價值，以及我們實現這些資產出售或解決的獲利能力，進而影響我們的流動性。儘管我們已實施風險管理策略，以及設計用以管理市場利率變動相關風險的政策與程序，但無法保證我們能成功管理利率風險。如果未來借款者或存款者行為或整體經濟狀況與我們預期的有顯著差異，則我們的風險緩釋措施可能不足以保護我們免受利率風險影響，進而對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生不利影響。
重大或持續的經濟衰退可能導致我們的不良貸款與租賃水平增加，或減少對我們產品與服務的需求，這可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。

本公司業務與營運成果受金融市場與總體經濟狀況影響，包括利率水平與波動性、通貨膨脹、住宅價格、失業率與失業率、破產率、家庭收入與消費支出等因素。我們在一個不確定的經濟環境中運作，原因包括但不限於貿易政策與爭議、關稅、地緣政治緊張與全球軍事衝突，包括俄羅斯與烏克蘭戰爭與中東衝突、通貨膨脹、商品價格波動與全球供應鏈與能源市場價格與中斷。在經濟成長放緩或成長緩慢的時期，與本公司業務相關的風險會更加嚴重。此外，由於本公司貸款中大量貸款是以加州與紐約的不動產為擔保，本公司特別容易受到這些州經濟衰退的影響。
